#| label: setup
#| include: false

# Shared by every chapter. Kept in one place so the experiment a figure refers
# to is never ambiguous, and so a change of configuration re-renders everything
# that depends on it rather than some of it.
from __future__ import annotations

import matplotlib
matplotlib.use("Agg")

import pandas as pd

from vision_zero import viz
from vision_zero.data import load_codebook
from vision_zero.modeling.config import load_experiment
from vision_zero.modeling.dataset import build_dataset, load_compiled

pd.set_option("display.max_columns", 50)
pd.set_option("display.width", 120)


def _hide_index_in_rendered_tables() -> None:
    """Stop the row index appearing as an unlabelled first column.

    Every table in this book is assembled row by row from a list of
    dictionaries, so its index is a running count from zero that carries no
    information. Rendered, it appears as a leading column of bare integers that
    reads like data and invites a reader to wonder what it means.

    Set once here rather than by wrapping each table at the point of use, so
    that a table added later cannot forget to do it. A frame that genuinely
    wants its index shown can call `.reset_index()` to make it a real column.
    """
    original = pd.DataFrame._repr_html_

    def without_index(self: pd.DataFrame) -> str | None:
        # A RangeIndex is the automatic one and never means anything. An index
        # the caller set deliberately is left alone.
        if isinstance(self.index, pd.RangeIndex):
            return self.to_html(index=False, border=0, na_rep="")
        return original(self)

    pd.DataFrame._repr_html_ = without_index  # type: ignore[method-assign]


_hide_index_in_rendered_tables()

BOOK = load_codebook()

#: The headline experiment: Montreal, three severity levels, reports with at
#: most one blank field. Argued for in @sec-quality.
EXPERIMENT = load_experiment("montreal_ternary_complete")
